summary: Puffin Island Light Station: a granite light first shown on 1 March 1873 off Greenspond in Bonavista Bay, its tower replaced around 1950, and still on the staffed-lightstation list.

lens.note: Fourth-order Chance Brothers Fresnel lens, supplied with the 1872-73 lighthouse (LighthouseFriends)

structures.type: granite tower attached to a keeper's dwelling
structures.note: Built 1872-73 by Smith and Haw; torn down in 1950 (LighthouseFriends)

structures.type: square wooden pyramidal tower with a two-storey frame dwelling
structures.note: Replacement after the granite tower came down; Rowlett dates the present station 1951

staffing.note: Named on the Fisheries and Oceans Canada list of staffed lightstations (page modified 2019); LighthouseFriends says it is still staffed

access.note: Staffed lightstation and keepers' home. LighthouseFriends: grounds open, tower closed. Rowlett: site open, tower closed, accessible only by boat, with a good view from Greenspond.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (owner per LighthouseFriends; site manager per Rowlett)

events.note: Smith and Haw build the granite lighthouse and attached dwelling on the island
Fixed red light first shown 1 March 1873; first keeper Robert Kelland Oakley
Fall gales and heavy seas made the water supply unusably salty; fresh water brought by boat
Light changed from fixed red to occulting white
Keeper Edward Wheeler rowed out to a schooner in a gale and guided her to anchorage inside Greenspond harbour
Granite tower torn down and replaced by a frame dwelling and square wooden pyramidal tower (Rowlett dates the present station 1951)
A keeper drowned shortly after leaving the island by kayak
Canadian Coast Guard announced plans to de-staff the staffed lighthouses in Newfoundland and Labrador and British Columbia; Senate committee recommended the plan be halted
Polar bear near the station on 3 April 2012 (LighthouseFriends, citing CBC News); keepers took shelter

notes_for_editor: KEEPERS: LighthouseFriends is the only list of keepers; the sources give no roles beyond 'keeper', so role is 'keeper'. Names are as LighthouseFriends prints them. Post-1960 keepers (Herron, Wakeley, Bragg) are named only as LighthouseFriends prints them, with no personal detail; the 2001 drowning is in the story without a name. NOT JOINED: Fred William Oakley (1875-1897) and Frederick William Oakley (1901-1904) may be one man. SOURCE LIMITS: the history rests on LighthouseFriends, which quotes Newfoundland inspectors' reports (Oke 1866, Nevill 1872, 1876, 1889) from the Journal of the House of Assembly and similar; those primary reports were not reachable from our corpus, so the story attributes them to LighthouseFriends. The Canadian Department of Marine reports in the corpus begin in 1900 and Newfoundland joined Canada only in 1949, so they do not cover this station's early years. Greenspond Historical Society's 'Puffin Island Lighthouse' page repeats LighthouseFriends almost word for word and is not counted as a second source. Linda White's 1997 history is the only independent history used. CONFLICTS LEFT OPEN: (a) the present station's date: LighthouseFriends says the granite tower was torn down in 1950; Rowlett gives 1951 for the station and keeper's house; the record gives 1951 for the tower. (b) Characteristic: the Coast Guard list gives Fl W 5s (flash every five seconds, which LighthouseFriends also describes); Rowlett gives white light 2.5 s on, 2.5 s off, i.e. occulting. The record uses Fl W 5s. (c) Tower height: LighthouseFriends gives 4.9 m; Rowlett gives 8 m (25 ft) for the square pyramidal wood tower; the record gives 8.0 m from Wikidata; the CCG list has a column near 4.9 that is not clearly labelled. Not corrected here. (d) Focal height: CCG 21.0 m and Rowlett 21 m agree with the record; the 1873 light's focal plane was 25.9 m (LighthouseFriends). (e) Staffing: DFO's list is a page modified 2019; CCG list is undated; LighthouseFriends says 'still staffed' with no date. The record's staffing check remains open. (f) Access: LighthouseFriends says grounds open and tower closed; Rowlett says site open, tower closed, boat only; the record says boat only and restricted. NOT RESEARCHED: Newfoundland newspapers and the Journal of the House of Assembly (not reachable through our tools); the 2011 Senate report 'Seeing the Light' (cited through LighthouseFriends only); the 1938 Barrelman item LighthouseFriends cites for Wheeler; the 2012 CBC article. Wikipedia not used. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-28: story corrected on the fact-check pass (quote fidelity; second-hand Nevill and Oke quotes marked as quoted by LighthouseFriends; the Greenspond and DFO wording tightened; a Rowlett access sentence now matches the directory).
